newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Police guard streets as strike grips Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: Police guard streets as strike grips Bangladesh.

text.p: Hundreds of police and paramilitary troops on Thursday guarded streets and key installations in the Bangladesh capital Dhaka as an opposition-led strike virtually paralysed the country, police and officials said.

Police said the government deployed more than 5,000 police and troops in Dhaka to prevent any violence by supporters of the main opposition Bangladesh nationalist Party (BNP), which called the work stoppage to protest higher taxes levied in the budget.
The strikers halted all road transportation except for rickshaws. Many Dhaka residents were seen walking to work.
Communication ministry officials said most trains and launches had moved out of their terminals in the early morning.
But they said hundreds of people were stranded as inter-district bus services had been suspended by the strike. "The road communications have been badly affected," one official said.
"There has been no violence so far. But the BNP workers are yet to take to the street to enforce the strike," a police officer said.
The BNP of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia called Thursday's work stoppage to protest what it says is an "anti-people" budget passed by parliament on Monday.

The BNP had sought the withdrawal of a 2.5 percent infrastructure development tax on imports and some locally produced goods and services, which Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria proposed when unveiling the budget last month.
BNP Secretary General Abdul Mannan said on Tuesday -- the first day of Bangladesh's fiscal 1997/98 year -- that the budget was against the interests of the country.
"The budget will deter investment and it will make the country dependent on others," he told party supporters.
